newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia discusses possible Seita investment.
newsitem.headline: Serbia discusses possible Seita investment.

text.p: Serbia will foster strategic partnerships with foreign investors to push the economy forward, privatisation minister Milan Beko told a delegation of French businessmen on Thursday.

Beko met representatives of the French tobacco company Seita which appears interested in investing in Yugoslavia's tobacco industry, the Serbian Information Ministry said in a statement faxed to Reuters on Friday.
Seita officials will visit several Yugoslav tobacco factories before deciding on its investment plans, the statement said.

"Serbia's government will particularly support programmes in which investors appear as strategic partners who will bring to our firms and market new technology and quality management and whose financial strength will allow realisation of the firms' development programmes," it quoted Beko as saying.
To qualify for the government support, investment deals must contain a long-term development strategy and foreigners are expected to offer an adequate social programme.

So far, Serbia has struck only one major strategic partnership deal, selling a 49 percent stake in its Telekom Srbija to Italian and Greek companies Stet and OTE for almost $1 billion. The deal guarantees job security to employees for a total of five years.
There was noone immediately available for comment at the privatisation ministry.
